name: player_keeptradecut_value as_of_month_day anchors each year row on the chosen calendar day (executed-result parity)
description: The as_of_month_day param replaces the NFL opening day as the year-axis as-of boundary, resolving to the same calendar day within each row's own year. Anchor selection, the 30-day recency floor and the outer future clamp are all the same expression feeding one lookup, so one seeded population covers all three. Two columns differing only by year_offset supply the past and future anchors: column _0 anchors at 2025-06-15 (past) and column _1 at 2055-06-15, which the outer LEAST(..., now()) must clamp to now. The offset is what makes the future arm time-robust -- a literal future YEAR is unreachable, because the row-axis year list is capped at the current season, and LEAGUE_MOCK_DATE cannot move this boundary either since the clamp compares against Postgres now() rather than the JS clock. Two pids: 920001 carries an observation 5 days inside the 2025 anchor window AND one 5 days before now, so it resolves on both columns; 920002's ONLY observation predates the 2025 window by 75 days, so it must read NULL on both. The second pid is what makes the floor mutation falsifiable -- with both observations on one pid, MAX(observed_at) <= boundary selects the in-window row whether or not the floor is applied, and that mutation would stay green. Goes red under three separate mutations: dropping as_of_month_day from the request (column _0's anchor reverts to the 2025-09-04 opening day, so 920001 reads NULL instead of 3000), removing the two lower_bound_sql lines (920002 reads 1500 instead of NULL on column _0), and removing the outer LEAST(..., now()) (column _1's boundary stays at 2055-06-15 and 920001 reads NULL instead of 4000).
